meaning: The workload reached Kubernetes but one or more pods were waiting for target-provided config, mounts, certificates, or setup.
next_action: Turn the missing target condition into a target fact, preflight, lifecycle route, or better base variant.

meaning: The rendered objects refer to custom resource types that were not present on the target.
next_action: Use a CRD-owning base, preinstall the CRDs, or record an explicit no-CRDs support boundary before rerun.

meaning: The objects applied, but a controller or workload did not become healthy in the observation budget.
next_action: Inspect pod logs/events, decide whether the issue is target policy, lifecycle, chart configuration, or a better base, then rerun.

meaning: The base deliberately expects a Secret or TLS material that was not staged on the target.
next_action: Stage the declared Secret or TLS material as a target fact, then rerun the local live and parity lanes.

meaning: The target could not pull at least one rendered image, so the row is testing image availability rather than ConfigHub parity.
next_action: Pin, mirror, override, or document the image dependency, then rerun against a target that can pull it.

meaning: The receipt shows stale namespace or cleanup interference, so the next useful step is a clean rerun.
next_action: Delete the stale namespace or rerun on a fresh cluster with an isolated namespace.

meaning: Kubernetes rejected an object because of permissions, admission, immutability, or API validation.
next_action: Decide whether the base needs a permission/admission preflight, a different target scope, or a rejected support boundary.

meaning: The chart expects provider credentials, cloud APIs, buckets, DNS, volumes, or another external system.
next_action: Model the provider dependency as target facts or an external managed prerequisite before rerun.
